message:
feat(update): wire the credential through both hops, and re-check the owner before sending

The primitive from the last commit is now called by the product. The chain
is: the application builds a snapshot, names a pipe, creates it before the
child, launches, and serves the credential to the process it holds a handle
for; the bootstrap receives it, opens its own pipe, keeps the working copy's
handle for the whole exchange, and hands it on; the worker builds an
endpoint from it and attaches it per request.

Two hops because the launch has two, and because the handle the application
holds is the bootstrap's. The bootstrap used to close that handle and leave
immediately -- with it closed, the process id it would compare against is
pinned to nothing, which is the exact state the comparison exists to refuse.

The client gets its own pipe name rather than one derived from the ready
event, because the client deliberately has no ready event: it is not
elevated and does not wait for permission to leave. A channel that carries a
credential still needs an identity even when nobody is waiting on anything.

That changes what the client does, and it is worth saying: it used to launch
the elevated process and walk away. It now stays for the exchange. What
keeps "stays" from becoming "hangs" is the deadline, not good behaviour from
the other side.

The owner is re-read at the moment of sending rather than reused from the
snapshot built before the consent prompt. If the user signed out or changed
servers while deciding, the attempt belongs to nobody: nothing is sent, the
worker fails its fetch, and no update is installed on behalf of someone who
is no longer there. Putting an epoch number in the message would not have
established this -- the check has to happen where the current state is.

Nothing happens before the credential arrives. A worker that does not
receive one exits before the effects run, so it never signals ready and
never stops the product.

Still missing, and not to be read as nearly done: the three-process
two-pipe regression (the primitive's checks are driven, but not across a
real bootstrap and worker), observation of the headers on the wire, and a
check that no fixture token reaches an environment block or a log -- only
the argument list is asserted so far.
